990 Efile Data Catalog

Form 990 and 990-EZ filers · release efile_v3_1

The NCCS 990 Efile database turns the XML returns that nonprofits file electronically with the IRS into 131 relational tables, one or more for each Part of Form 990, Form 990-EZ, and their Schedules. Every table is published for each tax year in two formats, CSV and Parquet.

Release efile_v3_1 (published 2026-10-09)
Returns Form 990 and Form 990-EZ, with schedules
Tax years 2009–2025 (2025 is a partial year)
Tables 131 tables, 2,126 table-year files
Filings 6,307,836 returns
Labels concordance990 2.0.3
Private foundations Form 990-PF returns are a separate database: efilepf_v3_1 catalog

About this release

Data sources and processing

IRS 990 e-file returns are published by the IRS as XML documents. NCCS builds this database from the XML files indexed by the Giving Tuesday 990 Data Commons, supplemented with returns the IRS e-file index lists but the Data Commons index never picked up (see the release notes below).

Each XML element (xpath) is assigned to a research variable and a table by the Master Concordance (concordance990), and the tables are built with the ef2 package. A table holds one Part of a form or schedule: either one row per filing (1:1), or several rows per filing for repeating groups such as officers, grants, or program service accomplishments (1:M).

Efile data are organized by tax year, the closest approximation to the calendar year in which the nonprofit’s activities took place. The tax year (TAX_YEAR) is the year in which the fiscal year begins (TAX_PERIOD_BEGIN_DATE). Returns are due five months after the fiscal year ends, and the IRS releases them in monthly batches, so the most recent tax year is always incomplete and keeps growing for two to three years.

Every table carries the keys needed to join tables to each other and to the BMF: OBJECTID (OID- followed by 18 digits, one per filing), EIN2, and TAX_YEAR. One-to-many tables add TABLE_ID (TID-NNN-NNN-NNN, one per row). Every row also carries URL, a link to the source XML return: open it to confirm whether a value is missing from the return or was not captured by the concordance.

R packages

  • ef2 Parses IRS 990 e-file XML into the relational tables published here.
  • concordance990 The Master Concordance: maps XML xpaths to variables and tables; holds the data dictionaries.
  • panel990 Downloads efile tables and builds longitudinal panels, with BMF fields attached.
  • fiscal Fiscal health accounting metrics from 990 data.
  • governance Governance scores for nonprofits from Part VI.
  • peopleparser Splits officer and director names into parts and infers gender.
  • titleclassifier Classifies officer titles into standard roles.

An archive of historic 990 forms and schedules is available from the Nonprofit Open Data Collective.

Coverage

Before tax year 2021, electronic filing was required only for the largest nonprofits (more than $10 million in assets) and for private foundations. Other organizations adopted it gradually. Beginning with tax year 2021 (calendar year 2022), e-filing is mandatory for almost all tax-exempt organizations, so recent waves cover nearly the full population of 990 and 990-EZ filers. For earlier years, the larger an organization is, the more likely it filed electronically; sample weights can be built by comparing efilers with the BMF or the NCCS Core files.

Table and file names

Table names follow the pattern FF-PPP-TTT-NAME, and each file appends the tax year: F9-P07-T01-COMPENSATION-2023.parquet.

  • FF is the form: F9 = Form 990, SA = Schedule A, SB = Schedule B, and so on.
  • PPP is the part: P01 = Part I, P02 = Part II, and so on. P00 is the heading and P99 holds lines outside any part or from earlier versions of the form.
  • TTT is the table: T00 holds the one-to-one fields of the part, and T01, T02, … are its one-to-many tables.

Tables whose names end in -EZ hold lines that appear only on Form 990-EZ. All other tables pool the matching lines from the 990 and the 990-EZ.

Each table-year is published as CSV (readable anywhere) and Parquet (smaller and much faster in R with arrow or duckdb; panel990 reads Parquet by default). Both files hold the same rows and columns. Table-years with no filings are omitted from the listings below.

Release notes

Changes from efile_v2_3 to efile_v3_1. Generated by ef2::write_release_notes() on 2026-10-09.

Notes

  • New filings. This release adds filings that the Giving Tuesday Data Commons (GTDC) index never listed. The IRS e-file index lists 184,165 such filings (990, 990-EZ and 990-PF; IRS batches 2025_09A, 2025_10A, the second half of 2026_05A, and 2026_08A). Their XML is re-hosted at https://nccs-efile.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/xml2/v2_3_patch/<OBJECT_ID>_public.xml, with PATCH-INDEX-v2_3-2026-10-07.csv beside them. The build index combined the GTDC index of 2026-08-25 with that patch, one row per filing.
  • TY2025 is new: built from the combined index. Many TY2025 returns are not filed yet, so expect it to grow.
  • Labels follow concordance990 2.0.1 (commit 02de916). Relabelling moved some xpaths between tables; where the builders already selected those cells by xpath, the published tables are unchanged.
  • Keys. OBJECTID is OID- + 18 digits, and TABLE_ID is the fixed-width TID-NNN-NNN-NNN (EF2-17), in every table.
  • Record. dev/UPSTREAM-ISSUES.md (EF2-18) in the ef2 repository documents how this release was built and checked.
  • Header table. F9-P00-T00-HEADER gains F9_00_ORG_EXEMPT_TYPE (EF2-12): the filer’s tax-exempt status as one string (501c3, 501c4, …, 4947a1, 527), derived from the 501(c) subsection attribute and the status checkboxes.

Summary

  • Tax years: 2009-2025 (previously 2009-2024).
  • Tables: 0 added, 0 dropped.
  • Table-years in both releases: 2,000; row counts changed in 391, column counts in 18; rows fell in 0.
  • Columns: 10 added and 0 removed, across 3 tables.
  • Filings: 6,307,836, previously 5,981,036 (+326,800).
  • Concordance: 59 xpaths newly mapped, 0 dropped, 187 moved between tables, 0 variables renamed, 0 multi_value changes.

Release notes on S3

Version history

Every release stays on S3 and keeps its catalog page, so earlier analyses can be reproduced. Interim releases were built and posted but not announced as full public releases.

Release Returns Published Status Tax years Tables Filings Notes

Available tables

Each table lists its files by tax year. The code below each table uses panelize() from panel990 to download a multi-year panel of the table with BMF organization fields (NTEE codes, geography, subsection) attached.

Anchor your code to a release. panelize() reads the current release (efile_version()) unless told otherwise, so the same code returns different data after the next release. For reproducible results, name the release explicitly:

panel <- 
  panelize( tables = "F9-P01-T00-SUMMARY",
            years = 2020:2024,
            source = data_source( version = "v3_1" ),
            bmf = TRUE )

BMF fields come from the current NCCS master BMF. To fix those as well, save the BMF once and pass the data frame or file path to bmf =.
